title: The 0-COAST: no coast
intro: Make Noise, a Eurorack maker from Asheville, North Carolina, released the 0-COAST in 2016, a synth of its own rather than a module for a case. It takes from both of the 1960s schools of synthesis without following either: a keyboard-style oscillator and envelope from the East Coast (Moog), and from the West Coast (Buchla) harmonics added by a waveshaper and folder rather than filtered away, and a low-pass gate in place of a filter and amplifier. Make Noise called the result “no coast” synthesis.

timeline.name: Make Noise 0-COAST
timeline.text: One triangle-core oscillator, OVERTONE and MULTIPLY to add harmonics, BALANCE, the DYNAMICS low-pass gate, SLOPE and CONTOUR, Voltage MATH, a clock, stepped random and two channels of MIDI to CV, with 29 patch points and no filter.

timeline.name: Firmware update
timeline.text: A November update added portamento synced to the clock and editing of the program pages by MIDI CC.

timeline.name: Make Noise Strega
timeline.text: A later Make Noise desktop instrument, made with Alessandro Cortini: an oscillator, a degrading delay, a filter, a function generator and touch plates, built for textures.

relatives.name: Buchla Music Easel
relatives.text: The West Coast half of the idea: a complex oscillator with a wavefolder (TIMBRE) and low-pass gates in place of a filter and amplifier. This app plays it.

relatives.name: Buchla 292 lowpass gate
relatives.text: The module the 0-COAST’s DYNAMICS is compared to: a filter and amplifier moved by one control, built with vactrols, where the 0-COAST uses transistors.

relatives.name: Behringer MODEL D
relatives.text: The East Coast half: the Minimoog’s oscillators, ladder filter and contour generators. This app plays its recreation.

note: None of the databank’s records name the 0-COAST yet.
